reasoning: There are no state-specific 2026 general-election Senate or presidential polls for Washington, DC in the last 45 days from major outlets or pollsters; DC is overwhelmingly Democratic by structure (Cook PVI D+44), and in practice its federal general elections are lopsided for Democrats, but there is no fresh, DC-focused 2026 polling margin to quantify that advantage right now. National and generic-ballot polling over the last month show Democrats with a modest lead nationally, but those are not DC-specific and thus cannot be used as direct measures of the 2026 DC Senate or presidential margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report / Cook Partisan Voting Index (summary via Wikipedia)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index lists Washington, D.C. as D+44 at the statewide level, indicating it votes about 44 percentage points more Democratic than the national average in recent presidential elections.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling (reported by The Hill)
sources.details: A national Emerson College generic congressional ballot poll found Democrats leading Republicans by 11 points, 53% to 42%, indicating a Democratic advantage nationally but not specific to Washington, D.C.

sources.name: Reuters/Ipsos August 2026 Poll
sources.details: A Reuters/Ipsos national poll measured views on President Trump and the 2026 midterms using a representative U.S. sample, providing national but not DC-specific electoral sentiment.

sources.name: Civiqs approval polling (reported via Yahoo News)
sources.details: A large-sample Civiqs survey of Trump’s job approval showed in Washington state (not DC) 28% approval and 67% disapproval, illustrating regional disapproval but not applicable as DC-specific electoral polling.
